sources.publisher: CoinDesk Live at Ripple Swell 2026; transcript capture
claims: Brad Garlinghouse said Ripple Treasury handled $13T of 2025 payments and about 99.9 percent did not touch crypto rails or stablecoins.
He said Ripple Prime handled about $3T to $4T, with more than 99 percent off-chain.
He said one percent of $16T equals $160B and that Ripple would measure its on-chain conversion share in 2027.
He said about half of RLUSD was on XRPL and about half on Ethereum.
He said Ripple wants to drive XRP liquidity, utility and trust; he characterized Coinbase as exchange-led, Circle as stablecoin-led and Ripple as bridging traditional finance and blockchain.
limitations: This is a secondary transcript capture of a CoinDesk interview video.
Figures are executive estimates, not audited asset-level data.
The $160B is scenario arithmetic, not an XRP forecast or committed amount.
The RLUSD chain-split statement conflicts with provider snapshots and remains unverified.

sources.publisher: XRP Insights — Week 44 RLUSD chain-supply snapshot
claims: The indexed Oct31 report gives total RLUSD supply around $2.42B.
It attributes about $707M to XRPL and $1.71B to Ethereum, or roughly 29 percent on XRPL.
limitations: Page could not be opened directly in this run; figures are from the indexed public summary.
Provider contract/account inclusion and frozen or treasury balance treatment require raw-chain reconciliation.
This differs from other providers and the CEO statement.

claims: Oct29 XRPL total stablecoin market capitalization was reported at $1.069B.
RLUSD dominance was reported at 91.48 percent of XRPL stablecoin capitalization.
Those two fields imply about $978M RLUSD on XRPL; this is a derived estimate, not a direct displayed RLUSD supply figure.
limitations: The $978M is calculated from two dashboard fields.
Different cutoff and methodology from XRP Insights and the CEO interview.
Not a direct issuer-account or ERC20 contract read.

sources.publisher: Stablecoin Insider — RLUSD stablecoin guide, updated Oct27
claims: The guide reports approximately $2.59B total RLUSD supply, attributed to DefiLlama.
It reports about $1.02B on XRPL and $1.57B on Ethereum, implying roughly 39.4 percent on XRPL.
limitations: Rounded figures and date differ from the Oct31 XRP Insights snapshot.
Does not reconcile the difference with the CEO estimate.

sources.publisher: Standard Chartered — RLUSD custody and planned LMAX collateral integration
claims: Standard Chartered says institutional custody for RLUSD issued on XRPL is live for eligible clients through its DIFC branch regulated by DFSA.
Standard Chartered is working with Ripple and LMAX to make RLUSD eligible collateral using a collateral-mirroring model that does not require transfer of the underlying RLUSD to the venue.
limitations: The live service is RLUSD custody, not native XRP custody.
LMAX collateral mirroring remains subject to documentation, testing, regulation and internal approvals.
No custody balances, collateral utilization or client counts are disclosed.

sources.publisher: LMAX Group — Ripple partnership and RLUSD collateral integration
claims: LMAX and Ripple announced a multi-year partnership to integrate RLUSD as a core collateral asset across institutional trading infrastructure.
Ripple committed $150M in financing to LMAX.
The Jan15 announcement described RLUSD collateral and settlement integration and Ripple Prime connectivity with LMAX Digital.
The Oct12 LMAX update with Standard Chartered describes collateral mirroring as planned and subject to documentation, testing and approvals.
limitations: The later Oct12 update confirms the collateral-mirroring feature was still planned, not live.
The $150M is corporate financing to LMAX, not an XRP purchase or XRP reserve allocation.
No RLUSD collateral balances, XRP trading volumes or venue-level asset inventory are disclosed.
